claims.statement: Optional secondary local graph viewer: knowledge-view-export projects one exact-revision explain or impact neighborhood into a bounded JSON or offline HTML view, knowledge-view-render displays a separately attributed view JSON, and the HTML page lets a person inspect records and edges, try a temporary hypothetical premise, and copy a question back to the primary coding-agent conversation.

attributes.decision_changed: Whether a task needs the viewer at all: the agent can answer from sources without an index or browser, so reach for a view only when visual inspection of a bounded neighborhood helps.
attributes.claim_ceiling: Documented role of merged source (PR #761); browser use and agent benefit not established.

claims.statement: knowledge_view.py projects, structurally validates and renders a GraphExplorationView v1 envelope from query records or curated JSON, using the packaged offline graph_view.html asset. The CLI commands that invoke it live in semantic_cli.py, owned by component:semantic-cli.

attributes.claim_ceiling: Source inspected at 6f54a4a; nothing was executed.

claims.statement: The graph viewer stays secondary and without authority. The coding-agent conversation is the primary interface and needs no browser or index. A view is a bounded presentation, not reviewed knowledge: the browser does not fetch remote content, authenticate, update the reviewed graph, edit strategy, run agents, change source evidence or transmit a message. A hypothetical scenario or copied question only invites investigation; a changed assumption is not a proven change in any linked judgment, a plain references edge is not a necessary premise, and a graph miss is NOT_ASSESSED. Durable knowledge changes go through the normal reviewed process.

attributes.decision_changed: Rejects changes that make the viewer a required step, a graph-authoring surface, a host-integrated action trigger or evidence for a conclusion.
attributes.authority_note: The design reports owner agreement in conversation on 2026-11-05; no separate owner record or ADR for the viewer was inspected, so this is recorded as document authority, not owner authority.

claims.statement: At 6f54a4a, the view code enforces only mechanical boundaries. The builder and validator reject any view or query whose semantic_truth_established or action_authorized is not false; export and render are create-only and refuse output under .sensemaking/knowledge; edge role is CONTEXT_ONLY for references and contained_in and UNKNOWN otherwise; the HTML asset has no fetch, XMLHttpRequest, remote script or innerHTML use, and scenario and copy state live only in page memory. Validation does not check that a cited source entails an interpretation, and a non-mechanical, non-lexical indexed record is labelled SOURCE_DECLARED without an original-source check.

attributes.claim_ceiling: Source reading and text search only; browser behavior was not run.
attributes.staleness_condition: Re-inspect when knowledge_view.py, graph_view.html or the knowledge-view commands in semantic_cli.py change.

claims.statement: At 6f54a4a, the repository records for the viewer that PR #761 head 37809b7 passed hosted Release Candidate Distribution and Semantic Context Re-entry, while Product Validation reported 3,634 passed and one failed, attributed to an older receipt enum. Local unit and synthetic tests, browser interaction, an isolated installed-wheel CLI run, independent later-agent use and comparative creative benefit remain NOT_RUN or NOT_ASSESSED. A text search of tests/, .github/ and scripts/ finds no reference to knowledge_view or knowledge-view; indirect coverage is not assessed.

attributes.claim_ceiling: Records what the documents state; the hosted run logs were not inspected.
attributes.staleness_condition: Supersede when a browser, installed-wheel or independent-agent run is recorded.

attributes.scope: Only the knowledge-view-export and knowledge-view-render commands
knowledge-view-export calls query_knowledge; knowledge-view-render reads a supplied view JSON and does not need an index
The design names ADR 0029 as governing: no deterministic planner or authority expansion, and the UI is not a master interface
